sentences.zh: 休斯顿及其郊区非常引人注目，因为像许多郊区一样，过去十年里这里经历了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: And those demographic changes have chiefly benefited the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而这些人口结构的变化主要使民主党受益。

sentences.en: Seats that had never been winnable before for the party suddenly were competitive.
sentences.zh: 那些以前对该党来说从未有胜算的席位突然变得具有竞争力了。

sentences.zh: 在2020年大选前，休斯顿的地图看起来是这样的。

sentences.en: There were three solidly Republican seats, three solidly Democratic seats, and four seats that were more up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 有三个稳固的共和党席位，三个稳固的民主党席位，以及四个竞争激烈的席位。

sentences.en: So in theory, the Democrats in the Houston area could have won more seats than the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 所以理论上，休斯顿地区的民主党人本可以赢得比共和党人更多的席位。

sentences.en: But in redrawing the maps, the Republican-controlled state legislature did what's known as packing.
sentences.zh: 但在重划地图时，共和党控制的州议会采取了所谓的“打包”策略。

sentences.en: They redrew the lines and stuffed as many Democratic voters into the Democratic districts as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们重划了界线，尽可能多地将民主党选民塞进民主党选区。

sentences.en: And the result is the Democrats now actually have four safe Democratic seats, more than the three they had before.
sentences.zh: 结果是民主党现在实际上拥有四个安全的民主党席位，比之前的三个多了。

sentences.en: But the Republicans have seven safe seats.
sentences.zh: 但共和党拥有七个安全席位。

sentences.en: And there are absolutely zero swing districts left.
sentences.zh: 而且现在绝对没有摇摆选区了。

sentences.en: But what type of Republican or Democrat will win.

sentences.zh: 阿门。

sentences.en: Christian Collins himself is the first to take the stage.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安·柯林斯本人是第一个登上舞台的人。

sentences.en: I will proudly stand with you to stand with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 我将自豪地与你们站在一起，支持特朗普总统。

sentences.en: And I'm looking forward to seeing him back in the White House in 2024.
sentences.zh: 我期待着在2024年看到他重返白宫。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: He's a far-right candidate, and it's very clear that this is a far-right rally.
sentences.zh: 他是一位极右翼候选人，而且很明显这是一场极右翼集会。

sentences.en: He sets up the race as bigger than him, as ultimately about Donald Trump and getting him back into office.
sentences.zh: 他将这场竞选提升到超越他个人的高度，归根结底是关于唐纳德·特朗普以及如何让他重返办公室。

sentences.en: But first, it starts with taking back Congress.
sentences.zh: 但首先，一切要从夺回国会开始。

sentences.en: And then, he acknowledges the role that redistricting might play in that.
sentences.zh: 然后，他承认了选区划分在其中可能发挥的作用。

sentences.en: And the question for this district, Congressional District 8, is not whether we will elect a Republican, because we will.
sentences.zh: 对于这个选区，即国会第八选区，问题不在于我们是否会选出一名共和党人，因为我们肯定会。

sentences.en: It's what type of Republican.
sentences.zh: 问题是选出哪种类型的共和党人。

sentences.en: This race isn't about me versus the other guy or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选不是关于我与对手或其他什么人的较量。

sentences.en: This race is about the people versus the Washington establishment.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选是关于人民与华盛顿建制派的较量。

sentences.en: It may not be totally clear, but this is actually, at least indirectly, the first reference of many to come to Dan Crenshaw,
sentences.zh: 可能不太明显，但这实际上——至少是间接地——是未来多次提到丹·克伦肖的第一次，

sentences.en: who just three years in is now himself being branded the establishment.
sentences.zh: 他才上任三年，现在自己也被贴上了建制派的标签。

sentences.en: Along with other mainstream Republicans, like the Republican House leader, Kevin McCarthy,
sentences.zh: 与其他主流共和党人一样，比如共和党众议院领袖凯文·麦卡锡，

sentences.en: Crenshaw has endorsed Collins' opponent, Morgan Luttrell, who sort of looks like the kind of candidate you would create in a conservative fantasy lab.
sentences.zh: 克伦肖支持了柯林斯的对手摩根·卢特雷尔，他看起来就像那种你在保守派幻想实验室里创造出来的候选人。

sentences.en: But he's another former Navy SEAL, and his twin brother was the basis for the movie Lone Survivor.
sentences.zh: 但他也是前海豹突击队队员，他的孪生兄弟是电影《孤独的幸存者》的原型。

sentences.en: And like Collins, Luttrell is a very conservative candidate.
sentences.zh: 和柯林斯一样，卢特雷尔也是一位非常保守的候选人。

sentences.en: But Collins is using Crenshaw's endorsement as an attack line on Luttrell.
sentences.zh: 但柯林斯正利用克伦肖的支持作为攻击卢特雷尔的手段。

sentences.en: We do not need leaders that are going to go along to get along with the Washington establishment.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要那些为了与华盛顿建制派相处融洽而随波逐流的领导人。

sentences.en: That say conservative things when they're running, and then go and do just the opposite when they get elected.
sentences.zh: 那些在竞选时说保守派言论，当选后却做着截然相反事情的人。

sentences.en: And it's not a coincidence that this rally isn't even being held in the district that Collins is running in.
sentences.zh: 而且这场集会甚至没有在柯林斯参选的选区举行，这并非巧合。

sentences.en: It's actually in the district that Dan Crenshaw is running in.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是在丹·克伦肖参选的选区举行的。

sentences.en: Basically, this whole rally has been staged to ask voters, do you want another Crenshaw in office?
sentences.zh: 基本上，整场集会都是为了问选民：你们想让另一个克伦肖上台吗？

sentences.en: I want to thank you.
sentences.zh: 我想感谢你们。

sentences.en: God bless you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你们。

sentences.en: God bless Texas.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: God bless America.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑美国。

sentences.en: Thank you, guys.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Hi, my name's Shane.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫肖恩。

sentences.en: Do you have a moment to chat?
sentences.zh: 你有时间聊聊吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I'm a reporter with The New York Times out here in Texas.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的记者，现在在德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: Tell me your name and...
sentences.zh: 告诉我你的名字，还有……

sentences.en: Sherry Lindsey.
sentences.zh: 雪莉·林赛。

sentences.en: Sherry Lindsey.
sentences.zh: 雪莉·林赛。

sentences.en: How do you spell it?
sentences.zh: 怎么拼写？

sentences.en: S-H-A-R-I.
sentences.zh: S-H-A-R-I.

sentences.en: S-H-A-R-I.
sentences.zh: S-H-A-R-I.

sentences.en: We spoke to Sherry Lindsey and her husband, Jim.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了雪莉·林赛和她的丈夫吉姆。

sentences.en: They're in their 70s, and they own a couple of businesses in the Houston area.
sentences.zh: 他们七十多岁了，在休斯顿地区拥有几家企业。

sentences.en: And they're quite familiar with the candidates in this race.
sentences.zh: 他们对这场竞选中的候选人非常熟悉。

sentences.en: Morgan Luttrell.
sentences.zh: 摩根·卢特雷尔。

sentences.en: We know him.
sentences.zh: 我们认识他。

sentences.en: He's a friend of our family's.
sentences.zh: 他是我们家的朋友。

sentences.en: Who is?
sentences.zh: 谁是？

sentences.en: Luttrell.
sentences.zh: 卢特雷尔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so?
sentences.zh: 那又怎样？

sentences.en: Good person.
sentences.zh: 是个好人。

sentences.en: But not the...
sentences.zh: 但不是……

sentences.en: He's in the establishment.
sentences.zh: 他是建制派的。

sentences.en: We want them out.
sentences.zh: 我们要把他们赶走。

sentences.en: Sherry's concern comes not so much from Luttrell himself, but from the people who are supporting him.
sentences.zh: 雪莉的担忧与其说是来自卢特雷尔本人，不如说是来自支持他的人。

sentences.en: Who are you thinking of?
sentences.zh: 你指的是谁？

sentences.en: Crenshaw, for one.
sentences.zh: 克伦肖，首先就是他。

sentences.en: He's teamed up with Luttrell and several others.
sentences.zh: 他和卢特雷尔以及其他几个人联手了。

sentences.en: So we feel like they're more of the rhino establishment that's been in there, and that's the change that we want.
sentences.zh: 所以我们觉得他们更像是那种一直盘踞在那里的“伪共和党人”建制派，而这正是我们想要改变的地方。

sentences.en: We're tired of the same people getting in, saying they're going to do this.
sentences.zh: 我们厌倦了同样的人上台，说着他们会做这做那。

sentences.en: And don't do it.
sentences.zh: 结果却什么都不做。

sentences.en: I mean, he's been around a while, but Crenshaw, so...
sentences.zh: 我是说，他已经在政坛混了一段时间了，但克伦肖，所以……

sentences.en: When we asked the Lindseys what specific votes Crenshaw had taken that were so worrisome, they dug around for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 当我们问林赛夫妇克伦肖具体投了哪些令人担忧的票时，他们翻找了一会儿。

sentences.en: Well, gun control, for one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，枪支管制，首先就是这个。

sentences.en: And mentioned gun control.
sentences.zh: 提到了枪支管制。

sentences.en: And this came up in a couple of conversations.
sentences.zh: 这在几次谈话中都提到了。

sentences.en: Crenshaw, he is an okay dude.
sentences.zh: 克伦肖，他是个还不错的家伙。

sentences.en: Not my politics.
sentences.zh: 但政治立场和我不同。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's not your politics about him?
sentences.zh: 他哪里的政治立场和你不同？

sentences.en: A lot of people call him a rhino.
sentences.zh: 很多人叫他“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: I would have to agree.
sentences.zh: 我不得不表示同意。

sentences.en: Reese Johnson is an 18-year-old college freshman.
sentences.zh: 里斯·约翰逊是一位18岁的大一新生。

sentences.en: He's just not voting in the way that we as, you know, constituents would want him to vote.
sentences.zh: 他只是没有按照我们，你知道，选民希望他投票的方式去投票。

sentences.en: So what are some of the things that you feel like he has done or said in terms of his votes that you disagree with?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得他在投票方面做了或说了哪些你不同意的事情？

sentences.en: Specifics, ooh.
sentences.zh: 具体细节，噢。

sentences.en: I was more well-versed on this when it happened, but, you know.
sentences.zh: 事情发生时我对此了解得更清楚，但是，你知道的。

sentences.en: I have to say it was, was it the gun control?
sentences.zh: 我得说是，是枪支管制吗？

sentences.en: It was something about constitutional carry that he wasn't coming out as strongly as he could about that.
sentences.zh: 是关于宪法赋予的持枪权，他在那件事上没有表现出应有的强硬态度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的。

sentences.en: What Reese and the Lindseys are both referring to is the fact that after two back-to-back mass shootings in 2019, including one at a Walmart in El Paso that left dozens dead,
sentences.zh: 里斯和林赛夫妇提到的都是同一个事实：在2019年连续发生两起大规模枪击事件后，包括埃尔帕索沃尔玛超市那起导致数十人死亡的事件，

sentences.en: Crenshaw had signaled at least some openness to red flag laws.
sentences.zh: 克伦肖至少表现出对“红旗法案”持开放态度。

sentences.en: Laws that would take guns away from people who are determined by a judge to be a threat to themselves or others.
sentences.zh: 该法律旨在从被法官认定对自己或他人构成威胁的人手中收缴枪支。

sentences.en: This is something that other Republicans also said that they might be open to at the time, including President Trump.
sentences.zh: 当时其他共和党人也表示可能对此持开放态度，包括特朗普总统。

sentences.en: In fact, it was his lead, Crenshaw said he was following.
sentences.zh: 事实上，克伦肖说他是跟随特朗普的领导。

sentences.en: The legislation never ended up going anywhere, and Crenshaw maintains an A rating from the NRA.
sentences.zh: 这项立法最终不了了之，而克伦肖在全国步枪协会（NRA）仍保持着A级评分。

sentences.en: But it was something that voters were using to point at something deeper, a kind of gnawing suspicion that Crenshaw has turned out to be a rhino, Republican in name only.
sentences.zh: 但这被选民用来指向更深层的问题，即一种挥之不去的怀疑：克伦肖原来是个“伪共和党人”（RINO）。

sentences.en: And at the rally, the source of that idea was pretty easy to trace.
sentences.zh: 而在集会上，这种观点的来源很容易追溯。

sentences.en: What we cannot have is weak-spined Republicans or rhinos in office.
sentences.zh: 我们不能容忍软弱的共和党人或“伪共和党人”在位。

sentences.en: We also need to defeat communist rhinos like Crenshaw, Kinsinger, and the people they support.
sentences.zh: 我们还需要击败像克伦肖、金辛格以及他们所支持的人那样的共产主义“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: If you didn't stand for the tens of millions of Americans that stand for liberty, we will expose you for being a Republican in name only, a rhino.
sentences.zh: 如果你不为数千万支持自由的美国人挺身而出，我们就会揭露你只是名义上的共和党人，一个“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: And possibly even recruit someone to run against you.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能招募人选来与你竞争。

sentences.en: We are seeing that promise through, believe me.
sentences.zh: 我们正在兑现这一承诺，相信我。

sentences.en: We are exposing Dan Crenshaw and the other fraud Republicans, wrapping themselves in President Trump's America First message to sneak into office.
sentences.zh: 我们正在揭露丹·克伦肖和其他欺诈性的共和党人，他们披着特朗普总统“美国优先”的外衣混入政府。

sentences.en: But the voters won't be fooled.
sentences.zh: 但选民不会被愚弄。

sentences.en: We know how to spot a rhino from a mile away.
sentences.zh: 我们一眼就能认出“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: You know the old saying, if it looks like a duck, walks like a duck, and quacks like a duck, then it's probably a duck.
sentences.zh: 你知道那句老话，如果它看起来像鸭子，走起来像鸭子，叫起来像鸭子，那它很可能就是鸭子。

sentences.en: Well, in today's Republican politics, if it talks like a rhino, is friends with rhinos, and takes money from rhinos.
sentences.zh: 那么，在今天的共和党政治中，如果他说话像“伪共和党人”，和“伪共和党人”交朋友，还拿“伪共和党人”的钱。

sentences.en: Well, my friends, what are they?
sentences.zh: 那么，我的朋友们，他们是什么？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I've learned a lot about our local guys, our new district, Dan Crenshaw, that I didn't know about Dan.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我了解了很多关于我们当地人、我们新选区、丹·克伦肖的事情，这些我以前都不知道。

sentences.en: And I come in here and hear these guys talking about him, and I'm like, wow, that's really true, man.
sentences.zh: 我来到这里，听到这些人谈论他，我就想，哇，那真是真的，伙计。

sentences.en: I just, he's not, you know, he's tricked us.
sentences.zh: 我只是，他不是，你知道，他欺骗了我们。

sentences.en: He's played the usual game of trickery with us, and he's not what he purports himself to be.
sentences.zh: 他跟我们玩了惯用的欺骗游戏，他并不是他所标榜的那样。

sentences.en: And now he actually represents us in this district.
sentences.zh: 而现在他竟然代表我们这个选区。

sentences.en: It's shocking.
sentences.zh: 这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, it's quite shocking.
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上，这相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: What's shocking about it?
sentences.zh: 哪里令人震惊？

sentences.en: With Dan, you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是说丹吗？

sentences.en: With Dan Crenshaw, specifically?
sentences.zh: 具体指丹·克伦肖吗？

sentences.en: Um, that, um, that he's, that he's not, that he's not what he purports to be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他，嗯，他不是，他不是他所标榜的那样。

sentences.en: I don't think that he is.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他是。

sentences.en: Specifically?
sentences.zh: 具体指什么？

sentences.en: I had a pretty good opinion of him in the beginning, but the more I see, the more I hear, and I'm changing that opinion.
sentences.zh: 起初我对他的评价还不错，但看得越多，听得越多，我正在改变这种看法。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It was something that was resounded by all the speakers up there.
sentences.zh: 台上所有的演讲者都表达了同样的观点。

sentences.en: You know, if you know, he's a rhino.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果，你知道，他是个“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: That's what, that's what I'm hearing.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所听到的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, I can't say that for certain, but it's certainly, you know, it's kind of like if it smells like a duck, walks like a duck, talks like a duck, quacks, it's a duck.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不能肯定地说，但这当然，你知道，就像如果它闻起来像鸭子，走起来像鸭子，说起来像鸭子，叫起来像鸭子，那它就是鸭子。

sentences.en: So, I'm beginning to think it's a duck.
sentences.zh: 所以，我开始认为他就是只鸭子。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But again, no one was really providing specifics about what it was that made Crenshaw so problematic.
sentences.zh: 但同样，没有人真正提供关于是什么让克伦肖变得如此成问题的具体细节。

sentences.en: As Shane said, it was just kind of like establishment vibes.
sentences.zh: 正如肖恩所说，这只是一种建制派的氛围。

sentences.en: It was clearly not primarily an issue with his politics or his policy views, which, again, are quite conservative.
sentences.zh: 显然，这主要不是关于他的政治立场或政策观点的问题，因为这些观点再次强调，是非常保守的。

sentences.en: What can I do for you?
sentences.zh: 我能为你做些什么？

sentences.en: My name's Shane.
sentences.zh: 我叫肖恩。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I just wanted to talk to you about what, do you mind if we record stuff here?
sentences.zh: 是的，我只是想和你谈谈，你介意我们在这里录音吗？

sentences.en: Then we spoke with Dee Scott, a 70-year-old realtor who lives in the area.
sentences.zh: 然后我们采访了迪·斯科特，一位住在该地区的70岁房地产经纪人。

sentences.en: What do you think of Crenshaw as a Republican?
sentences.zh: 你认为克伦肖作为一名共和党人怎么样？

sentences.en: Is he the kind of person you're looking for somebody to emulate or not?
sentences.zh: 他是那种你希望别人效仿的人吗？

sentences.en: I think Dan Crenshaw might possibly be a rhino.
sentences.zh: 我认为丹·克伦肖可能是一个“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: Might possibly be a rhino.
sentences.zh: 可能是一个“伪共和党人”。

sentences.en: What about?
sentences.zh: 关于什么？

sentences.en: So, this will pretty much tell you where I stand, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想这基本上能告诉你我的立场。

sentences.en: The first time that I heard him say, as far as the, here we go, the election being stolen,
sentences.zh: 我第一次听到他说，关于，开始了，选举被窃取，

sentences.en: that has nothing to do with anything, that was not the case, just forget about it, it never took place, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 那与任何事情都无关，事实并非如此，忘了它吧，它从未发生过，等等等等。

sentences.en: And there's so much evidence coming out that it did take place.
sentences.zh: 而且现在有这么多证据表明它确实发生了。

sentences.en: It's the first time in my life that I've not trusted our government, that I've not trusted elections,
sentences.zh: 这是我一生中第一次不信任我们的政府，不信任选举，

sentences.en: and I am just searching to find some way to determine who's the best to put in office to keep this country going forward and still be a great country.
sentences.zh: 我只是在寻找某种方法来确定谁是最好的人选，能让这个国家继续前进，并依然保持伟大。

sentences.en: What Dee's talking about is Dan Crenshaw's stance on the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 迪所说的是丹·克伦肖在2020年大选上的立场。

sentences.en: So, he did initially cast doubt on the election, getting involved in a Texas lawsuit that had asked the Supreme Court
sentences.zh: 他确实最初对选举表示怀疑，参与了一项德克萨斯州的诉讼，要求最高法院

sentences.en: to toss out the results in a few key swing states that Joe Biden had won.
sentences.zh: 推翻乔·拜登获胜的几个关键摇摆州的选举结果。

sentences.en: But when the Electoral College did certify the results, Crenshaw backed down, and he said his party needed to accept them and move on,
sentences.zh: 但当选举人团确认结果后，克伦肖退缩了，他说他的党派需要接受结果并继续前进，

sentences.en: making him one of the few Republicans willing to do so.
sentences.zh: 这使他成为少数愿意这样做的共和党人之一。

sentences.en: And he set himself even further apart in the aftermath of January 6th by saying that members of his own party were responsible for, quote, hyping up that day.
sentences.zh: 在1月6日事件之后，他通过表示他自己党内的成员应对“炒作那一天”负责，从而进一步将自己与他们区分开来。

sentences.en: Many members of Congress did do that.
sentences.zh: 许多国会议员确实那样做了。

sentences.en: Many commentators did do that.
sentences.zh: 许多评论员确实那样做了。

sentences.en: Many in the media have been doing that for the last few weeks, constantly, saying this is our time to fight.
sentences.zh: 许多媒体在过去几周里一直在这样做，不断地说这是我们战斗的时候了。

sentences.en: And let me tell you something very clearly.
sentences.zh: 让我非常清楚地告诉你们一件事。

sentences.en: They've been lying to people.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在对人们撒谎。

sentences.en: They've been lying to millions.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在欺骗数百万人。

sentences.en: They've been lying that January 6th was going to be this big solution for election integrity.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在撒谎说1月6日会成为选举公正性的重大解决方案。

sentences.en: It never was going to be.
sentences.zh: 它从来都不会是。

sentences.en: He said there was absolutely no way under the Constitution that Congress could possibly overturn the election results.
sentences.zh: 他说根据宪法，国会绝无可能推翻选举结果。

sentences.en: And they lied to people, and they said, go fight.
sentences.zh: 他们欺骗了民众，说去抗争吧。

sentences.en: Go fight, because everything's on the line.
sentences.zh: 去抗争吧，因为一切都危在旦夕。

sentences.en: That's what they said.
sentences.zh: 他们就是这么说的。

sentences.en: And when people fought, they came to fight.
sentences.zh: 当人们去抗争时，他们确实去抗争了。

sentences.en: And then they fought Capitol Police, and now people are dead.
sentences.zh: 然后他们与国会警察发生了冲突，现在有人死了。

sentences.en: And those same members of Congress who called people to fight, well, they were nowhere to be found because it was all fun and games to them.
sentences.zh: 而那些号召民众去抗争的国会议员们，却不见踪影，因为对他们来说，这一切不过是闹剧一场。

sentences.en: And most recently, Crenshaw's gone into a number of public disagreements with the right wing of his party that is most vocal about election fraud.
sentences.zh: 最近，克伦肖与他所在党派中那些对选举舞弊问题呼声最高的右翼派系发生了多次公开分歧。

sentences.en: An attack that was seen as being directed at the House Freedom Caucus, but which he has since tried to clarify was actually about specific members,
sentences.zh: 这次攻击被视为针对众议院自由核心小组，但他后来试图澄清，这实际上是针对特定成员的，

sentences.en: calling them performance artists and grifters.
sentences.zh: 称他们为表演艺术家和骗子。

sentences.en: It's this position on the 2020 election that's made him a number of enemies in Washington and in the conservative media, and that now seems to be driving the biggest wedge

sentences.en: between some Republican voters and Dan Crenshaw, like those at this Christian Collins rally.
sentences.zh: 一些共和党选民与丹·克伦肖之间最大的隔阂，比如在这次克里斯蒂安·柯林斯的集会上。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about your shirt and what it says?
sentences.zh: 能跟我说说你的衬衫以及上面写了什么吗？

sentences.zh: 好的，我的衬衫上写着：别怪我，我投给了特朗普。

sentences.en: And I hear that a lot from people that it's like, well, I voted.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到人们这么说，就像是，好吧，我投票了。

sentences.en: Another person we met at the rally is Phil Cady.
sentences.zh: 我们在集会上遇到的另一个人是菲尔·凯迪。

sentences.en: He's a former airline mechanic who told us that he left his job after the company announced a vaccine mandate.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名航空公司机械师，他告诉我们，在公司宣布疫苗强制令后，他辞职了。

sentences.en: He, too, was angry at Crenshaw for his position on the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 他也对克伦肖在2020年大选上的立场感到愤怒。

sentences.en: I don't think he really supported any kind of revisiting of the election.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他真的支持任何形式的重新审视选举。

sentences.en: You know, uh...
sentences.zh: 你知道，呃……

sentences.en: But also...

sentences.zh: ……在你看来。

sentences.zh: ……在1月6日的问题上也越界了。

sentences.en: January 6th.
sentences.zh: 1月6日。

sentences.en: Cady told us that he himself was at the Capitol on that day, though he says that he didn't go inside, but he feels Crenshaw has betrayed the people who were there.
sentences.zh: 凯迪告诉我们，他本人那天也在国会大厦，尽管他说他没有进去，但他觉得克伦肖背叛了当时在场的人。

sentences.en: Why hasn't he fought for the Texans to get out of jail?
sentences.zh: 为什么他没有为那些德州人争取出狱？

sentences.en: Why isn't he speaking up?
sentences.zh: 为什么他不站出来说话？

sentences.en: You know, why aren't our own Republicans standing up for the fraudulent elections?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么我们自己的共和党人不支持那些舞弊的选举？

sentences.en: We're trying to get them out.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图把他们救出来。

sentences.en: Just as President Trump is supporting candidates to unseat some of these other Republicans because they've lost their way.
sentences.zh: 就像特朗普总统支持候选人去取代这些共和党人一样，因为他们迷失了方向。

sentences.en: They've got no spine to stand up and do what's right for the people.
sentences.zh: 他们没有骨气站出来为人民做正确的事。

sentences.en: Phil is right.
sentences.zh: 菲尔说得对。

sentences.en: Donald Trump's singular litmus test for who he's going to support in the 2022 elections is all about whether or not they accepted the 2020 election results.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在2022年选举中支持谁的唯一试金石，就是他们是否接受2020年的选举结果。

sentences.en: In fact, at the end of January, when Trump came to Texas and had a rally just outside of Houston,
sentences.zh: 事实上，一月底特朗普来到德克萨斯州，在休斯顿郊外举行集会时，

sentences.en: he recognized a lot of the politicians in the crowd, calling them out by name, praising them.
sentences.zh: 他认出了人群中的许多政客，点名并称赞了他们。

sentences.en: There was just one congressman there who Trump noticeably left out.
sentences.zh: 现场只有一位国会议员被特朗普明显地冷落了。

sentences.en: Dan Crenshaw.
sentences.zh: 丹·克伦肖。

sentences.en: And I've since been told that was no accident.
sentences.zh: 后来有人告诉我，那并非偶然。

sentences.en: In the Republican Party today, there's really only one fault line that counts.
sentences.zh: 在今天的共和党内，真正重要的分歧线只有一条。

sentences.en: And it has nothing to do with policy.
sentences.zh: 而且这与政策毫无关系。

sentences.en: It's all about the question of Donald J.
sentences.zh: 这完全是关于唐纳德·J·

sentences.zh: 特朗普和选举舞弊的问题。

sentences.en: And are you with him or are you against him?
sentences.zh: 你是支持他还是反对他？

sentences.en: And for many, if you're against him, you're a rhino.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，如果你反对他，你就是“犀牛”（RINO，共和党内的民主党人）。

sentences.en: What is your sense of Dan Crenshaw?
sentences.zh: 你对丹·克伦肖有什么看法？

sentences.en: Rhino.
sentences.zh: “犀牛”。

sentences.en: We need to get him out.
sentences.zh: 我们需要把他赶走。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.zh: 你对丹·克伦肖有什么不满？

sentences.en: He's for this Cheney.
sentences.zh: 他支持这个切尼。

sentences.en: He's all for the big rhinos, the people that hate Trump.
sentences.zh: 他完全支持那些大“犀牛”，那些讨厌特朗普的人。

sentences.en: He's against the people that like Trump, like Marjorie Taylor Greene, who's supposedly here today.
sentences.zh: 他反对那些喜欢特朗普的人，比如今天应该也在场的玛乔丽·泰勒·格林。

sentences.en: So yeah, Crenshaw became a traitor to us.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，克伦肖成了我们的叛徒。

sentences.en: He hates Trump.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌特朗普。

sentences.en: In the kind of political coincidence that is rarely an accident, it wasn't much of a surprise that one of the speakers at the rally, in fact, the headliner,
sentences.zh: 在那种极少是巧合的政治巧合中，集会的一位演讲者，实际上是压轴嘉宾，并不令人意外，

sentences.en: is someone that Crenshaw has feuded with most publicly.
sentences.zh: 正是克伦肖公开争吵过的人。

sentences.en: Well, I will say I love all of you, too.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我也想说，我也爱你们所有人。

sentences.zh: 佐治亚州众议员玛乔丽·泰勒·格林。

sentences.en: Really excited.
sentences.zh: 真的很兴奋。

sentences.en: Texas is such a great state.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州真是个伟大的州。

sentences.zh: 绝对棒极了。

sentences.zh: 克伦肖甚至称她为白痴。

sentences.en: And the understanding was that she was one of the people he was referring to when he said that the party had been taken over by performance artists and grifters.
sentences.zh: 大家普遍认为，当他说党被表演艺术家和骗子接管时，她就是他所指的人之一。

sentences.en: But the reason why I'm here is for a very specific reason.
sentences.zh: 但我来这里是有非常具体的原因的。

sentences.en: It's time to draw a line in the sand.
sentences.zh: 是时候划清界限了。

sentences.en: Technically, Marjorie Taylor Greene was there to rally support for Christian Collins.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，玛乔丽·泰勒·格林是来为克里斯蒂安·柯林斯争取支持的。

sentences.en: But it was clear that she wasn't just thinking about this one district.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，她不仅仅是在考虑这一个选区。

sentences.en: She was talking about remaking the entire Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 她在谈论重塑整个共和党。

sentences.en: That whole Bush, Cheney wing of the party needs to go.
sentences.zh: 布什和切尼那一派的人必须走人。

sentences.en: And so as we're watching all this, I see how the incentive structures for politicians are changing in real time.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们观察这一切时，我看到了政客们的激励机制是如何实时变化的。

sentences.en: Not only has Trump's power and influence over the Republican Party created this litmus test, along which Republicans are now dividing, or a civil war,
sentences.zh: 特朗普对共和党的权力和影响力不仅创造了这个试金石，共和党人现在正沿着这条线分裂，或者说是一场内战，

sentences.en: as Marjorie Taylor Greene put it.
sentences.zh: 正如玛乔丽·泰勒·格林所说的那样。

sentences.en: But the redistricting process itself is reinforcing that.
sentences.zh: 而且选区重划过程本身也在强化这一点。

sentences.en: By the time all the lines are drawn this year, as many as 90% of congressional seats will only be competitive in the primaries, when only the most fervent voters tend to turn out,
sentences.zh: 到今年所有选区线划定之时，多达90%的国会席位将只在初选中具有竞争性，而初选通常只有最狂热的选民才会出来投票，

sentences.en: and where moderation and compromise are often punished.
sentences.zh: 在那里，温和与妥协往往会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: Now, that doesn't mean that redistricting guarantees that the most extreme candidates will win.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着选区重划保证了最极端的候选人会获胜。

sentences.en: But it does change the parameters of the debate.
sentences.zh: 但这确实改变了辩论的参数。

sentences.en: So in District 8, Christian Collins has centered his race on his support of Trump, and he has repeatedly spread the falsehood that the 2020 election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 所以在第8选区，克里斯蒂安·柯林斯将他的竞选重点放在了对特朗普的支持上，并反复散布2020年大选被窃取的谎言。

sentences.en: But his opponent, Morgan Luttrell, the candidate that Dan Crenshaw has endorsed, he's also supported that claim.
sentences.zh: 但他的对手，丹·克伦肖支持的候选人摩根·拉特雷尔，也支持这一说法。

sentences.en: All of which begs the question of whether it would even be possible for a candidate to run in this district with any other point of view.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都引出了一个问题：在这个选区，候选人是否还有可能持有其他观点。

sentences.en: And all of that made us very eager to talk to Dan Crenshaw himself.
sentences.zh: 这一切让我们非常渴望采访丹·克伦肖本人。

sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: And because the congressman's running late, Sue Walden, his political director, gives us a tour of the office.
sentences.zh: 由于议员迟到了，他的政治主管苏·沃尔登带我们参观了办公室。

sentences.zh: 特朗普总统。

sentences.en: And so, Crenshaw's relationship with Trump, it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以，克伦肖与特朗普的关系，很复杂。

sentences.en: And I'm getting excited to ask him about it.
sentences.zh: 我正兴奋地想问他这件事。

sentences.en: And just then, he walks in the door.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，他推门走了进来。

sentences.en: Congressman?
sentences.zh: 议员先生？

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Shane Goldmacher.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·戈德马赫。

sentences.en: Shane.
sentences.zh: 肖恩。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Thanks for making the time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Yeah, nice to meet y'all.
sentences.zh: 好，很高兴见到你们大家。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Diana.
sentences.zh: 你好，戴安娜。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: And so we go into this media room that has a big green screen where Crenshaw records a lot of his television appearances.
sentences.zh: 我们走进这间媒体室，里面有一块巨大的绿幕，克伦肖经常在这里录制电视节目。

sentences.en: Do you want coffee, Dan, or anything?
sentences.zh: 丹，你想喝咖啡还是别的什么吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if it's fine.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这行不行。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How long are we going to have?
sentences.zh: 我们有多少时间？

sentences.en: We sit down.
sentences.zh: 我们坐了下来。

sentences.en: He cracks open a 24-ounce sugar-free Monster Energy drink.
sentences.zh: 他打开了一罐24盎司的无糖魔爪能量饮料。

sentences.en: And we begin.
sentences.zh: 我们开始了。

sentences.en: Well, thanks for making the time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: I wanted to sort of start back in 2018 when you were first running for office and you first got elected.
sentences.zh: 我想从2018年你刚开始竞选公职并首次当选时谈起。

sentences.en: And you were pretty immediately tagged as a rising star in the Republican Party, the future of the party.
sentences.zh: 你当时很快就被贴上了共和党明日之星、党内未来的标签。

sentences.en: And I kind of want to know what you made of that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是怎么看待这些评价的。

sentences.en: What did you think people meant by that at that time?
sentences.zh: 你认为当时人们说这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: And what you represented that made you the future of the party at that moment?
sentences.zh: 你当时代表了什么，让你成为了党内的未来？

sentences.en: It's good.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: Jeez, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't really think about that question very often.
sentences.zh: 我并不常思考这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, I don't – it's all been a little bit surreal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我……这一切都有点超现实。

sentences.en: The allure has certainly worn off.
sentences.zh: 那种吸引力肯定已经消退了。

sentences.en: I'll say that much.
sentences.zh: 我只能说这么多。

sentences.en: What the future of the Republican Party should be is people who can make better arguments on the left.
sentences.zh: 共和党的未来应该是那些能对左派提出更好论点的人。

sentences.en: And what happens too often is it becomes a contest of who hates the left the moSt.
sentences.zh: 但经常发生的情况是，这变成了一场比谁更痛恨左派的竞赛。

sentences.en: That's not a persuasive argument.
sentences.zh: 那不是一个有说服力的论点。

sentences.en: And that's what I represented back then.
sentences.zh: 那是我当时所代表的。

sentences.en: That's what I represent now.
sentences.zh: 那也是我现在所代表的。

sentences.en: You know, it's – I don't think a lot has changed really.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这……我不认为真的改变了很多。

sentences.en: That's what got me famous, right?
sentences.zh: 那是我成名的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: It was, you know, this sort of moment on Saturday Night Live.
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道，在《周六夜现场》上的那个时刻。

sentences.en: And that's what I've tried to stick to, to the greatest extent possible.
sentences.zh: 这也是我一直试图尽可能坚持的东西。

sentences.en: I want to just ask you because I think the current conversation about where you fit in the Republican Party is pretty different today than it was in 2018.
sentences.zh: 我想问你，因为我认为关于你在共和党内定位的当前对话，与2018年时大不相同。

sentences.en: And it really seems like the reason revolves not about policy positions that you've taken or specific votes for the most part, but, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且看起来原因主要不在于你采取的政策立场或具体的投票，而是，你知道，

sentences.en: your relationship to Donald Trump and to sort of the Trumpism movement in general.
sentences.zh: 你与唐纳德·特朗普以及整个特朗普主义运动的关系。

sentences.en: And so I guess as I think about this, there's this key moment where you gave that speech in 2020 at the RNC.
sentences.zh: 我想，当我思考这个问题时，有一个关键时刻，就是你在2020年共和党全国代表大会上发表的那次演讲。

sentences.en: And you didn't – you didn't talk about him at all.
sentences.zh: 你根本没有提到他。

sentences.en: You didn't use his name.
sentences.zh: 你没有提到他的名字。

sentences.en: You talked about American heroes.
sentences.zh: 你谈论的是美国英雄。

sentences.en: And I wanted to know, you know, why not?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你知道，为什么不提？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, it's probably good to go to the RNC speech to explain this because it is a good example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，用那次共和党大会的演讲来解释这一点可能很好，因为它是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: And it's an example of the following.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于以下情况的例子。

sentences.en: There's a big difference between Trump and the Trump family and the movement around that.
sentences.zh: 特朗普、特朗普家族以及围绕他们的运动之间有很大的区别。

sentences.en: But so I have a good relationship with Trump and the Trump family.
sentences.zh: 但我与特朗普和特朗普家族关系很好。

sentences.en: You know, I think it's this manufactured division that there's some rift between me and Trump.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为我和特朗普之间存在某种裂痕，这是一种人为制造的分歧。

sentences.en: That's just not true.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是真的。

sentences.en: And the RNC speech is a good example of this because they tasked me with writing a speech about American heroes.
sentences.zh: 共和党大会的演讲就是一个很好的例子，因为他们指派我写一篇关于美国英雄的演讲稿。

sentences.en: They didn't say write a speech about the president.
sentences.zh: 他们没说要写一篇关于总统的演讲稿。

sentences.en: And then the little staffers got mad afterwards because we didn't talk about the president.
sentences.zh: 后来那些小职员们生气了，因为我们没谈到总统。

sentences.en: Why didn't you talk about the president?
sentences.zh: 为什么不谈谈总统？

sentences.en: Because you told us to write this speech.
sentences.zh: 因为你们让我们写的是这个演讲。

sentences.en: Like there's – so there's no conspiracy here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面没有什么阴谋。

sentences.en: Like there's no there there.
sentences.zh: 根本没那回事。

sentences.en: It's just this silliness.
sentences.zh: 这只是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: Can I ask you about – you said you have a great relationship with him.
sentences.zh: 我能问你关于——你说你和他关系很好。

sentences.en: Yeah, what is your – are you guys in touch or what is – yeah, how would you describe your relationship?
sentences.zh: 是的，你们之间——你们有联系吗，或者是什么——是的，你会如何描述你们的关系？

sentences.en: I talked to him recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近和他谈过。

sentences.en: I went to the rally here in Houston recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近去了休斯顿的集会。

sentences.en: I spoke with him on the phone with me and Kevin McCarthy and him a week before that.
sentences.zh: 在那之前一周，我和凯文·麦卡锡还有他通过电话。

sentences.en: I had a cordial conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一次友好的交谈。

sentences.en: He's always hearing things, right, because look, I have enemies, of course, on the right.
sentences.zh: 他总是听到各种传言，对吧，因为你看，我当然有敌人，在右翼阵营里。

sentences.en: That's what you're getting at effectively.
sentences.zh: 这正是你想要表达的意思。

sentences.en: And look, it's – that's the establishment that doesn't want people like me to rise too quickly.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是那些不想让像我这样的人崛起得太快的建制派。

sentences.en: What's the establishment?
sentences.zh: 什么是建制派？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: I'm going to explain that because I view the establishment differently than what most people say the establishment is.
sentences.zh: 我要解释一下，因为我对建制派的看法与大多数人所说的不同。

sentences.en: Most people say the establishment is Kevin McCarthy and Mitch McConnell and the RNC.
sentences.zh: 大多数人说建制派是凯文·麦卡锡、米奇·麦康奈尔和共和党全国委员会。

sentences.en: That's not the establishment.
sentences.zh: 那不是建制派。

sentences.en: They're trying to hang on by a thread.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图垂死挣扎。

sentences.en: They're trying to wrangle cats.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图去管教那些难以驾驭的人。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？

sentences.en: That's what leadership is doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是领导层正在做的事情。

sentences.en: The establishment is these sort of wannabe social media influencers, these radio hosts, these podcasters.
sentences.zh: 建制派是那些想当网红的社交媒体影响者、电台主持人和播客主。

sentences.en: It's mostly these folks in the media that are so ingrained in the cancel culture of the right.
sentences.zh: 主要是媒体里那些深深沉迷于右翼“取消文化”的人。

sentences.en: That's what I'm fighting againSt.
sentences.zh: 那才是我正在对抗的。

sentences.en: And they view me as a threat because I don't really toe the line in the way that they want.
sentences.zh: 他们视我为威胁，因为我没有完全按照他们想要的方式去随波逐流。

sentences.en: Whatever it is they want, it's funny because it's hard to – it's hard to discern what makes them different and who them really is.
sentences.zh: 无论他们想要什么，这很有趣，因为很难分辨是什么让他们与众不同，以及他们到底是谁。

sentences.en: We're all the same.
sentences.zh: 我们都是一样的。

sentences.en: We all believe the same things.
sentences.zh: 我们都相信同样的事情。

sentences.en: So it's this manufactured divisions.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是人为制造的分歧。

sentences.en: There's no policy differences really between people who label themselves conservative, people who label themselves America first, people who label themselves MAGA.
sentences.zh: 在那些自称保守派、自称“美国优先”、自称MAGA的人之间，其实并没有政策上的分歧。

sentences.en: But there is a big difference now, right?
sentences.zh: 但现在确实有很大的不同，对吧？

sentences.en: The big difference that really seems to be dividing the Republican Party is do you say and believe that the 2020 election was stolen?
sentences.zh: 真正分裂共和党的大分歧是：你是否说并相信2020年大选是被窃取的？

sentences.en: I think that's less of an issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为那不是主要问题。

sentences.en: I mean it bubbles up every once in a while.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它偶尔会冒出来。

sentences.en: We get it at questions about it, concerns.
sentences.zh: 我们会收到关于它的提问和担忧。

sentences.en: But it's – look, we also do polling.
sentences.zh: 但你看，我们也做民调。

sentences.en: So we get a much wider swath of the population and it does not rank very high.
sentences.zh: 所以我们能接触到更广泛的人群，而这个问题排名并不高。

sentences.en: This is not what people have asked about over the last year.
sentences.zh: 这不是过去一年里人们一直在问的问题。

sentences.en: People are much more concerned about inflation and the border crisis, things like that.
sentences.zh: 人们更关心通货膨胀和边境危机之类的事情。

sentences.en: So it's – I'm not saying – I agree that it's inflation and the border is a bigger issue for voters.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是说——我同意通货膨胀和边境问题对选民来说更重要。

sentences.en: I guess it's almost become like table stakes to be a real Republican now.
sentences.zh: 我想这几乎成了成为一名真正共和党人的入场券了。

sentences.en: By polling, 70, 80 percent of the Republicans and 100 percent of the people I've met out here think the election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 根据民调，70%到80%的共和党人，以及我在这里遇到的100%的人，都认为选举是被窃取的。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to just ask when you talk about speaking out about performance artists and grifters, when you talk about taking on some part of the base of your party,
sentences.zh: 所以我想问，当你谈论要公开反对那些表演艺术家和骗子时，当你谈论要挑战党内基础的一部分时，

sentences.en: I want to ask you why.
sentences.zh: 我想问你为什么。

sentences.en: Because it's definitely not the easier pathway and it's definitely not the safer political pathway.
sentences.zh: 因为这绝对不是更容易的道路，也绝对不是更安全的政治道路。

sentences.en: So why are you doing it?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Well, again, I have to take a step back and say this isn't the battle that you kind of make it out to be.
sentences.zh: 好吧，再说一次，我得退后一步说，这并不是你所描述的那种战斗。

sentences.en: It's just so much less dramatic than that.
sentences.zh: 它远没有那么戏剧性。

sentences.en: When people are polled, you have to take a lot of these things with a grain of salt.
sentences.zh: 当人们被调查时，你必须对很多事情持保留态度。

sentences.en: It has become sort of a reaction.
sentences.zh: 这已经变成了一种下意识的反应。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, I was stolen.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，被窃取了。

sentences.en: Some people mean different things by that.
sentences.zh: 有些人对此有不同的理解。

sentences.en: Some people mean, well, the media stole it by characterizing Donald Trump in the most nefarious of ways in a way that wasn't honest and true.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为，媒体通过以最邪恶的方式描述唐纳德·特朗普，以一种不诚实和不真实的方式窃取了选举。

sentences.en: And so some people mean it that way.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人是这个意思。

sentences.en: So it kind of depends and you've got to dig deeper into people's opinions.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于具体情况，你必须深入挖掘人们的观点。

sentences.en: And, again, is this the driving force for them?
sentences.zh: 而且，这真的是他们的驱动力吗？

sentences.en: My polling wouldn't suggest that it is.
sentences.zh: 我的民调结果并不支持这一点。

sentences.en: I know our media engagement wouldn't suggest that it is.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们的媒体互动数据也不支持这一点。

sentences.en: It wouldn't suggest that it's this big dramatic division the way a lot of people – I don't think it's a division in the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着它是许多人所说的那种巨大的戏剧性分裂——我不认为这是共和党内部的分裂。

sentences.en: I think that the base of the Republican Party thinks the last election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 我认为共和党的基础选民认为上次选举是被窃取的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But if I'm like, hey, guys, I'm not so sure about that, I'm still doing okay.
sentences.zh: 但如果我说，嘿，伙计们，我对此不太确定，我依然过得很好。

sentences.en: So that's why my conclusion is it's not as dramatic of an event or phenomenon as maybe some seem to think it is.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我的结论是，它并没有像有些人认为的那样是一个戏剧性的事件或现象。

sentences.en: And why do it?
sentences.zh: 那为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Well, I just – I stick to what's defensible.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只是——我坚持那些站得住脚的东西。

sentences.en: I stick to what I can say in all honesty is true.
sentences.zh: 我坚持那些我可以诚实地说出来是事实的东西。

sentences.en: And if that pisses people off, it pisses people off.
sentences.zh: 如果这让人们生气，那就让他们生气吧。

sentences.en: I'm usually pissing off people on the left.
sentences.zh: 我通常会让左派的人感到生气。

sentences.en: But sometimes I piss off people on the right.
sentences.zh: 但有时我也会让右派的人感到生气。

sentences.en: So, you know, in the end, it's truth is the North Star.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，归根结底，真理是北极星。

sentences.en: I mean, are there members of Congress that you think of as performance auditors and grifters?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有没有你认为属于表演艺术家和骗子的国会议员？

sentences.en: There are some.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些。

sentences.en: I will not name them on a New York Times podcast or interview.
sentences.zh: 我不会在《纽约时报》的播客或采访中点名他们。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's pretty clear I think there's some.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为很明显有一些这样的人。

sentences.en: I just wouldn't characterize the Freedom Caucus that way.
sentences.zh: 我只是不会那样去定义自由党团。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not as a whole.
sentences.zh: 不是作为一个整体。

sentences.en: And I told them that.
sentences.zh: 我也告诉过他们。

sentences.en: I think they know that.
sentences.zh: 我想他们知道这一点。

sentences.en: It was just sort of a kind of munching of words I think that occurred.
sentences.zh: 我想这只是某种措辞上的误解。

sentences.en: In any case, what I meant by grifters and liars were what I already talked to you about, right?
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我所说的骗子和骗徒就是我之前跟你谈过的那些人，对吧？

sentences.en: This sort of cabal of establishment that I was talking about who are trying to monetize division and outrage on the right.
sentences.zh: 就是我所说的那个建制派阴谋集团，他们试图利用右翼的分歧和愤怒来获利。

sentences.en: They manufacture divisions, again, by labeling people different things.
sentences.zh: 他们通过给人们贴上不同的标签来人为制造分歧。

sentences.en: They don't really know what the differences are as far as policy or what they stand for.
sentences.zh: 他们并不真正了解政策上的差异或他们所代表的立场。

sentences.en: They don't really go that deep.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有深入研究这些。

sentences.en: It's more a matter of style.
sentences.zh: 这更多是风格问题。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it happens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，这种事确实会发生。

sentences.en: It happens a lot more on the right and the left than I think it used to.
sentences.zh: 现在左右两派发生这种事的情况比以前多多了。

sentences.en: That's for sure.
sentences.zh: 那是肯定的。

sentences.en: I want to just go back to the thing on Trump because you were at the rally that was in your district.
sentences.zh: 我想回到特朗普那件事上，因为你当时就在你选区的集会上。

sentences.en: And he called out and recognized a lot of members of Congress who were there.
sentences.zh: 他点名并致意了当时在场的许多国会议员。

sentences.en: But he didn't recognize you.
sentences.zh: 但他没有提到你。

sentences.en: Was there any meaning behind that?
sentences.zh: 这背后有什么深意吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Could be, again, the staffers that I talked about because I just talked.
sentences.zh: 可能还是我刚才说的那样，是工作人员的问题，因为我只是去谈话的。

sentences.en: He invited me to the rally a few days before.
sentences.zh: 他几天前邀请我参加那个集会。

sentences.en: He also neglected to mention quite a few other people who were sitting there.
sentences.zh: 他也忽略了提到当时坐在那里的其他不少人。

sentences.en: I don't know if there were other members of Congress that didn't get mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我不知道还有没有其他没被提到的国会议员。

sentences.en: Louis Gohmert, it looks like they left him off the list as well.
sentences.zh: 路易·戈默特，看起来他们也没把他列入名单。

sentences.en: The only reason he got hit is because Trump was looking and he saw him.
sentences.zh: 他被提到的唯一原因是因为特朗普当时正好往那边看，看到了他。

sentences.en: Oh, Louis, what's up?
sentences.zh: 哦，路易，怎么样？

sentences.en: I don't think too much of it.
sentences.zh: 我没觉得这有什么大不了的。

sentences.en: I don't really care.
sentences.zh: 我其实不在乎。

sentences.en: And have you asked for his endorsement in 2022 or have you not asked Trump for your endorsement?
sentences.zh: 你有没有请求他在2022年为你背书，还是说你根本没找过特朗普寻求背书？

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't even know how that works.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我甚至不知道那套流程是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: I guess I haven't asked.
sentences.zh: 我想我没问过。

sentences.en: We're not even sure who to ask, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我们甚至不知道该找谁去问。

sentences.en: So the reason we're in Texas is it's the first state with midterms and all the districts in every state are getting redrawn.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以在德克萨斯州，是因为这是第一个进行中期选举的州，而且每个州的选区都在重新划分。

sentences.en: And the remapping here is, I think, particularly dramatic.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这里的重划特别剧烈。

sentences.en: Just in the Houston area, there were four seats that were competitive at the presidential election last cycle.
sentences.zh: 仅在休斯顿地区，上届总统选举时就有四个竞争激烈的席位。

sentences.en: And there are none now.
sentences.zh: 现在一个都没有了。

sentences.en: You used to have one of them now.
sentences.zh: 你以前拥有其中一个席位，现在没有了。

sentences.en: You don't.
sentences.zh: 你没有了。

sentences.en: And basically, with every single seat, you know, being wiped away, I wanted to ask you, when you get rid of competitive seats, like, what is the impact for democracy?
sentences.zh: 基本上，每一个竞争激烈的席位都被抹去了，我想问你，当你消除竞争性席位时，这对民主有什么影响？

sentences.en: This is a deeper political science question, and it's an interesting one to explore.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更深层的政治学问题，也是一个值得探讨的有趣问题。

sentences.en: Call it gerrymandering.
sentences.zh: 你可以称之为杰利蝾螈（不公正划分选区）。

sentences.en: Call it whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 随你怎么称呼都行。

sentences.en: I think highly politicized districts or highly partisan districts, deep red or deep blue, you can't ignore their contribution to some kind of division within the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为高度政治化或高度党派化的选区，无论是深红还是深蓝，你无法忽视它们对国家内部某种分裂所起的作用。

sentences.en: I think it exists, that contribution.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种作用是存在的。

sentences.en: However, if that were to be the case, then the same divisions wouldn't exist in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果真是这样的话，参议院就不应该存在同样的分裂。

sentences.en: And yet they do, almost in the exact same way.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，它们确实存在，而且方式几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: Can I push back, though, on the House and Senate districts?
sentences.zh: 我可以反驳一下关于众议院和参议院选区的说法吗？

sentences.en: Because let's go back to the election, right?
sentences.zh: 因为让我们回到选举，对吧？

sentences.en: I think it was 139 members of the House Republican Caucus voted not to certify the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 我想众议院共和党核心小组中有139名成员投票反对认证2020年选举结果。

sentences.en: A majority of your colleagues.
sentences.zh: 是你同事中的大多数。

sentences.en: But it was a small fraction of the Senate Republican Caucus that didn't vote to certify the election.
sentences.zh: 但参议院共和党核心小组中只有一小部分人没有投票认证选举结果。

sentences.en: It was, I don't know, the number, maybe eight, nine?
sentences.zh: 大概是，我不知道具体数字，也许八九个人？

sentences.en: I'm not sure that everything centers back to this certification of the election.
sentences.zh: 我不确定所有事情都归结于这次选举认证。

sentences.en: I don't think it necessarily does.
sentences.zh: 我不认为必然如此。

sentences.en: Because I'm looking at the aggregate over years.
sentences.zh: 因为我是在看多年来的总体情况。

sentences.en: That's one example of senators.
sentences.zh: 那只是参议员的一个例子。

sentences.en: Look, the Senate's always going to be slower and a little less extreme than the House.
sentences.zh: 听着，参议院总是会比众议院行动更慢，也稍微没那么极端。

sentences.en: But the divisions that we've seen throughout our country certainly exist in the Senate in a pretty serious way.
sentences.zh: 但我们在全国范围内看到的分裂，在参议院中确实以一种相当严重的方式存在。

sentences.en: So that's why I'm just saying, like, I'm not saying there's no effect from gerrymandering.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想说，我并不是说选区划分没有影响。

sentences.en: But I think it's much, much less than people give it credit for.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它的影响远没有人们想象的那么大。

sentences.en: Look, I think voters are self-sorting into these districts, too, right?
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为选民也在进行自我筛选，进入这些选区，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, inner Houston is all Democratic.
sentences.zh: 比如，休斯顿市区全是民主党人。

sentences.en: And exurbs are, like, more Republican than they used to be.
sentences.zh: 而郊区比以前更倾向于共和党。

sentences.en: But I do think people running statewide who have to take in cities, suburbs, and exurbs are behaving differently.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，那些必须涵盖城市、郊区和外围地区的州级竞选者，他们的表现方式是不同的。

sentences.en: I mean, you agree, too, that the districts are making some difference.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你也同意选区划分确实产生了一些影响。

sentences.en: But I do think, I just want to push back on that idea that it's not, that it's entirely the same in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，我只是想反驳那种认为参议院完全一样、没有区别的观点。

sentences.en: The Senate's, I mean, the Senate's different.
sentences.zh: 参议院，我是说，参议院是不同的。

sentences.en: But the Senate's different for some of those reasons.
sentences.zh: 但参议院的不同是有原因的。

sentences.en: It's pretty close.
sentences.zh: 这很接近了。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm just getting to the main point being that there's a lot of reasons for the sorting of America into left and right divisions.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的主要观点是，美国分裂成左右阵营的原因有很多。

sentences.en: Look, it is the urban-rural divide.
sentences.zh: 看，这就是城乡差距。

sentences.en: Suburbia has become the swing districts of America.
sentences.zh: 郊区已经成为了美国的摇摆选区。

sentences.en: The urban centers are unattainable for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 共和党人无法触及城市中心。

sentences.en: The rural districts are unattainable for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党人无法触及农村选区。

sentences.en: So that self-sorting has happened over the years.
sentences.zh: 所以这种自我筛选多年来一直在发生。

sentences.en: Social media has probably had a much greater role than any of these factors as far as the seething anger that Americans feel for each other.
sentences.zh: 就美国人对彼此感到的那种愤怒而言，社交媒体的作用可能比任何其他因素都要大得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, if I were to place one culprit on that, I would probably go with social media.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果我要找一个罪魁祸首，我可能会选社交媒体。

sentences.en: Gerrymandering has been around forever.
sentences.zh: 选区划分不公由来已久。

sentences.en: You're never going to get rid of political redistricting because there's not really a better option.
sentences.zh: 你永远无法摆脱政治选区重划，因为并没有更好的选择。

sentences.en: You're not going to have some formula.
sentences.zh: 你不可能搞出一个什么公式来。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just, it is what we have.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是我们所拥有的现状。

sentences.en: So we spend a lot of time complaining about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们花了很多时间抱怨它。

sentences.en: I mean, I always kind of laughed when left-wing Twitter would always post under any comment I made.
sentences.zh: 我是说，每当左翼推特在我发表的任何评论下发帖时，我总是觉得好笑。

sentences.en: They would post a picture of my district as if this was proof that I was somehow corrupt because my district is shaped funny.
sentences.zh: 他们会贴出我选区的形状，好像这就是我腐败的证据，因为我选区的形状很奇怪。

sentences.en: It's like I didn't draw it.
sentences.zh: 就好像是我画的一样。

sentences.en: I got into this job, you know, last year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是去年才开始做这份工作的。

sentences.en: And you guys are hammering for this.
sentences.zh: 你们却为了这个对我穷追猛打。

sentences.en: And also, what is it about the shape of a district that makes it corrupt?
sentences.zh: 而且，选区的形状到底哪里腐败了？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, really.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的吗？

sentences.en: Nobody thinks that through that next step.
sentences.zh: 没人会去深究那下一步。

sentences.en: And I just kind of find it funny as sort of a philosophical slash political science question.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这作为一个哲学或政治学问题很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: And it's just, in academic terms, why?
sentences.zh: 从学术角度来看，为什么？

sentences.en: And nobody can really answer that.
sentences.zh: 没人能真正回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, my old district was very ethnically balanced.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我以前的选区种族非常平衡。

sentences.en: It looked a lot like Texas looks.
sentences.zh: 它看起来很像德克萨斯州的样子。

sentences.en: And now my district doesn't look gerrymandered at all.
sentences.zh: 而现在我的选区看起来一点也不像被操纵过的。

sentences.en: Now my new district looks like a pond.
sentences.zh: 现在我的新选区看起来像个池塘。

sentences.en: My old one looked like a river running around Houston.
sentences.zh: 我以前的选区看起来像一条环绕休斯顿的河流。

sentences.en: What does your new district look like?
sentences.zh: 你的新选区看起来像什么？

sentences.en: Like a pond.
sentences.zh: 像个池塘。

sentences.en: Like it's, you know, it's just a normal looking shape.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，它只是一个正常的形状。

sentences.en: And so that's not, there's nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 所以这没什么问题。

sentences.en: But it's also not competitive, whereas my old district was.
sentences.zh: 但它也没有竞争性，而我以前的选区是有竞争性的。

sentences.en: Now, the real question.
sentences.zh: 现在，真正的问题来了。

sentences.en: With your new district, with the fact that it's not competitive, it is potentially competitive.
sentences.zh: 关于你的新选区，鉴于它没有竞争性，或者说潜在的竞争性。

sentences.en: It's just only competitive potentially in a Republican primary, right?
sentences.zh: 它只在共和党初选中才有潜在的竞争性，对吧？

sentences.en: There's basically no chance you're going to lose your seat to a Democrat in the next 10 years.
sentences.zh: 未来10年内，你基本上没有输给民主党人的可能。

sentences.en: And while you might not have said there was as much of a chance you would have lost to a Democrat in your old seat, it was at least conceivably possible.
sentences.zh: 虽然你可能不会说你在旧选区输给民主党人的几率有多大，但至少在理论上是有可能的。

sentences.en: I mean, what do you think it does for you personally that you can only be challenged from the right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你认为只能从右翼受到挑战，这对你个人意味着什么？

sentences.en: And then what does it mean for your party that so many people can only be challenged from the extremes in their parties?
sentences.zh: 这对你的党派又意味着什么，因为这么多人只能从党派极端派别那里受到挑战？

sentences.en: It changes nothing for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我没有任何改变。

sentences.en: Absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有任何改变。

sentences.en: And I'd be really interested to see what your findings are in about a year or two.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想看看你一两年后的调查结果。

sentences.en: Because the only way for you to, this will be the answer, really.
sentences.zh: 因为这才是真正的答案。

sentences.en: Because now that we've gone through this redistricting process and we've seen this great sorting throughout the country to the right and left districts.
sentences.zh: 因为现在我们经历了这次选区重划，看到了全国范围内向左右选区的这种大筛选。

sentences.en: So what you'll be able to then assess is that the members who went from a purple district like mine to a deep blue or a deep red,
sentences.zh: 所以你到时候就能评估，那些从像我这样的紫色选区转到深蓝或深红选区的议员们，

sentences.en: you'll be able to assess if their behavior radically changed.
sentences.zh: 你就能评估他们的行为是否发生了根本性的改变。

sentences.en: But, you know, the formal title also is representative, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，正式头衔也是“代表”，对吧？

sentences.en: So, like, are you going to represent your district?
sentences.zh: 所以，你是要代表你的选区吗？

sentences.en: So the math is that your old district was 1.5% Trump district in 2020, basically the equivalent of North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 数据是这样的：你以前的选区在2020年是1.5%的特朗普选区，基本相当于北卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: Your new district is 20, 23 percentage points for Trump, somewhere between Utah and Alabama.
sentences.zh: 你的新选区特朗普支持率高出20到23个百分点，介于犹他州和阿拉巴马州之间。

sentences.en: So, if you're going to be a representative, should you be changing, should you be considering changing, listening to these new constituents?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你要成为一名代表，你应该改变吗？你应该考虑改变吗？去倾听这些新选民的声音？

sentences.en: Again, I default to I think it's much deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 再一次，我还是认为这比那要深刻得多。

sentences.en: I don't think you're going to see a lot of formerly moderate members turn into radical leftists or radical right-wingers.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你会看到很多以前温和的议员变成激进的左派或激进的右翼分子。

sentences.en: I just don't think you're going to see that.
sentences.zh: 我只是不认为你会看到这种情况。

sentences.en: You're certainly not going to see it with me.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不会在我身上看到这种情况。

sentences.en: And not that I was ever moderate.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我曾经温和过。

sentences.en: That's kind of the big joke, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是那个大笑话，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just that I just don't yell and scream real loud.
sentences.zh: 只是我不会大喊大叫。

sentences.en: And somebody, well, you must be moderate.
sentences.zh: 然后有人会说，你一定很温和。

sentences.en: No, I just take a tone that doesn't turn people off.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是采取了一种不会让人反感的语气。

sentences.en: You should try it.
sentences.zh: 你应该试试。

sentences.en: You know, it works quite well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这非常有效。

sentences.en: That ain't going to change.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能改变的。

sentences.en: And I'm not a robot that just puts his, you know, licks his finger, puts it up to the wind and sees which way it's going and then votes accordingly.
sentences.zh: 而且我不是那种舔舔手指、看看风向、看风往哪吹就怎么投票的机器人。

sentences.en: That's not why you elected me.
sentences.zh: 你们选我不是为了这个。

sentences.en: You elected me because I said I stand for these sets of principles and I will make judgments accordingly.
sentences.zh: 你们选我是因为我说过我坚持这些原则，我会据此做出判断。

sentences.en: That's why you elected me, for my problem-solving capability, for my moral framework.
sentences.zh: 这就是你们选我的原因，为了我的解决问题的能力，为了我的道德框架。

sentences.en: That's what I ran on.
sentences.zh: 这就是我竞选的初衷。

sentences.en: At the Christian Collins rally over the weekend that was attended by Marjorie Taylor Greene and Madison Cawthorn and a slew of other people that have been critical of you,
sentences.zh: 在上周末的克里斯蒂安·柯林斯集会上，马乔里·泰勒·格林、麦迪逊·考索恩以及其他许多批评过你的人都出席了，

sentences.en: you know, you came up a lot, not just on stage, which I presume you've seen from the clips from Marjorie Taylor Greene and others.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你被提到了很多次，不仅仅是在台上，我想你已经从马乔里·泰勒·格林和其他人的视频片段中看到了。

sentences.en: But among the voters and the thing that they said and one person at the end really struck me because so many people called you a rhino and I'm sure you know this.
sentences.zh: 而且在选民中，最后一个人说的话真的触动了我，因为很多人称你为“共和党内奸”（RINO），我相信你知道这一点。

sentences.en: But the person at the end of the night that we talked to said he came in and he thought positively of you.
sentences.zh: 但那天晚上我们交谈的最后那个人说，他进来时对你的印象是积极的。

sentences.en: I don't know if he'd voted for you before.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他以前是否投过你的票。

sentences.en: He may not have been in your district.
sentences.zh: 他可能不在你的选区。

sentences.en: But he said, look, from what I'm hearing, he's a rhino.
sentences.zh: 但他确实说，看，从我听到的情况来看，他是个共和党内奸。

sentences.en: I'm hearing it all day.
sentences.zh: 我整天都在听这个。

sentences.en: And if it's, you know, talks like a duck and quacks like a duck and, you know, maybe it's a duck.
sentences.zh: 如果它走起来像鸭子，叫起来像鸭子，那它可能就是只鸭子。

sentences.en: And so I guess he's a rhino.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜他是个共和党内奸。

sentences.en: And so with these people with megaphones in your party calling you a rhino, what does that do as you're running?
sentences.zh: 那么，当党内这些拿着扩音器的人称你为共和党内奸时，这对你的竞选有什么影响？

sentences.en: I mean you face really token opposition this year.
sentences.zh: 我是说你今年面临的挑战微乎其微。

sentences.en: I think you've outraged anybody by 100 to 1.
sentences.zh: 我想你的得票率以100比1领先任何人。

sentences.en: But what does that do over time for a person who just a couple years ago was a future of the Republican Party figure that's not the kind of label that those people get?
sentences.zh: 但对于一个几年前还是共和党未来之星的人来说，随着时间的推移，这会产生什么影响？那可不是这些人通常会得到的标签。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean I don't really care.
sentences.zh: 我是说我真的不在乎。

sentences.en: I just don't really care.
sentences.zh: 我真的不在乎。

sentences.en: You know, it's chirping.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那只是叽叽喳喳的噪音。

sentences.en: It's chirping from, you know, from the fringe.
sentences.zh: 这声音是从，你知道的，从边缘地带传来的。

sentences.en: And it's sad.
sentences.zh: 而且这很可悲。

sentences.en: It's sad, right?
sentences.zh: 很可悲，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I see what you just described.
sentences.zh: 因为我看到了你刚才描述的那种情况。

sentences.en: I see it.
sentences.zh: 我看到了。

sentences.en: It's on social media.
sentences.zh: 它就在社交媒体上。

sentences.en: I see it with people.
sentences.zh: 我在人们身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Well, they said you're a rhino.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们说你是“共和党建制派”（RHINO）。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Well, then maybe don't take it at face value then if they can't even come up with a single example.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那如果他们连一个具体的例子都举不出来，也许你就别太当真了。

sentences.en: The quickest way to a conservative's heart is to call some other conservative a rhino.
sentences.zh: 赢得保守派好感的最快方法，就是指责其他保守派是“共和党建制派”。

sentences.en: That's the clickbait.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的点击诱饵。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: Well, conservatives have a natural concern about big government, a natural concern about people betraying them from their own side.
sentences.zh: 嗯，保守派对大政府有一种天然的担忧，对身边人背叛他们也有天然的担忧。

sentences.en: And so they're very susceptible to these kind of arguments.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很容易受到这类论调的影响。

sentences.en: You know, the fact that we even have a word for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们甚至专门造了个词来形容它。

sentences.en: You know, the Democrats just don't.
sentences.zh: 你知道，民主党人可不会这样。

sentences.en: They don't deal in this the way the right does.
sentences.zh: 他们不像右翼那样搞这一套。

sentences.en: And so, look, do I care?
sentences.zh: 所以，听着，我在乎吗？

sentences.en: No, not really.
sentences.zh: 不，其实并不在乎。

sentences.en: And, look, I wish more regular voters like the guy you talked about who supported me one second and then the next second didn't because, you know, he heard something.
sentences.zh: 而且，听着，我希望更多像你提到的那个人一样的普通选民，他上一秒还支持我，下一秒就不支持了，因为他听到了什么传言。

sentences.en: He's not sure what, but he heard something.
sentences.zh: 他不确定是什么，但他确实听到了什么。

sentences.en: I wish they would discern.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们能有辨别力。

sentences.en: I wish they would understand that that's the game, the trick being played on them.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们能明白这就是一场游戏，是别人在他们身上玩的把戏。

sentences.en: You started by saying you got into politics because you believe in making better arguments that can better persuade people to the Republican side.
sentences.zh: 你开头时说你投身政治是因为你相信通过提出更好的论点，能更好地把人们争取到共和党这边来。

sentences.en: And I guess I wanted to know with these new districts whether there are any House candidates who are Republican in Texas who have to care about that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在这些新的选区划分下，德克萨斯州还有没有共和党众议员候选人需要为此操心。

sentences.en: Like, you don't have to care about that.
sentences.zh: 比如，你根本不需要操心这个。

sentences.en: Your district doesn't sharpen your arguments anymore.
sentences.zh: 你的选区不再需要你磨练论点。

sentences.en: You don't need to sharpen your arguments to persuade the left.
sentences.zh: 你不需要磨练论点去说服左派。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: It's kind of sad, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这有点可悲，不是吗？

sentences.en: I still will because it's all I care about.
sentences.zh: 我依然会这么做，因为这是我唯一在乎的事情。

sentences.en: And, look, and if that doesn't win out, then the Republican Party is doomed.
sentences.zh: 而且，听着，如果这种理念不能胜出，那么共和党就完了。

sentences.en: But that philosophy needs to win out.
sentences.zh: 但这种理念必须胜出。

sentences.en: This idea that winning means persuading, that fighting means persuading, not just fighting for your own fundraising and fighting for the attention of the base.
sentences.zh: 这种理念就是：赢意味着说服，战斗意味着说服，而不是仅仅为了自己的筹款而战，也不是为了博取选民基层的关注而战。

sentences.en: You know, if that philosophy loses out, then there's no hope.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果这种理念输了，那就没有希望了。

sentences.en: I think Americans have to wake up to the fact that primaries matter.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国人必须意识到初选的重要性。

sentences.en: If I get an earful from plenty of Democrats that think AOC is an embarrassment to their party, okay, well, like how many people voted in that primary when she unseated Cowley?
sentences.zh: 如果我从很多民主党人那里听到抱怨，说AOC是他们党的尴尬，好吧，那当她击败Cowley时，有多少人参加了那场初选？

sentences.en: How many?
sentences.zh: 有多少？

sentences.en: Like nobody.
sentences.zh: 几乎没人。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, it's get involved in your primaries.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，要参与到你们的初选中去。

sentences.en: The same goes for both sides.
sentences.zh: 双方都是如此。

sentences.en: So, it's important.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很重要。

sentences.en: There are differences in people and honesty and integrity and experience.
sentences.zh: 人们在诚实、正直和经验方面是有差异的。

sentences.en: And you can't just assume that the best person is going to come out of a primary.
sentences.zh: 你不能理所当然地认为初选一定会选出最合适的人选。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: You've been super generous with your time.
sentences.zh: 你给了我很多时间，非常慷慨。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And nice to meet you in person.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能亲自见到你。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: And I would love to come back.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意再来。

sentences.en: Thanks, Wolf.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Wolf。

sentences.en: There's another big story that we're following tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们还在关注另一则重大新闻。

sentences.en: Results are coming in from the Texas primaries.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州初选的结果正在陆续出炉。

sentences.en: This is the first big contest of the 2022 election year, testing the influence of former President Trump on the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 这是2022选举年的第一场大战，考验着前总统特朗普对共和党的影响力。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, Texas held the first primaries of 2022.
sentences.zh: 周二晚上，德克萨斯州举行了2022年的首场初选。

sentences.en: And as expected, Dan Crenshaw won.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，Dan Crenshaw赢了。

sentences.en: Big.
sentences.zh: 大获全胜。

sentences.en: Drawing nearly 75% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 获得了近75%的选票。

sentences.en: The bastion of conservatism that is Montgomery County, the successor to Kevin Brady in Congressional District 8.
sentences.zh: 在蒙哥马利县这个保守主义堡垒，他是Kevin Brady在第8国会选区的继任者。

sentences.en: I was surprised by Luttrell.
sentences.zh: 我对Luttrell的表现感到惊讶。

sentences.en: He's up above 50% white right now.
sentences.zh: 他现在的得票率超过了50%。

sentences.en: Morgan Luttrell won his race, too, with more than twice as many votes as Christian Collins.
sentences.zh: Morgan Luttrell也赢得了他的竞选，得票数是Christian Collins的两倍多。

sentences.en: Both were decisive wins for the so-called establishment wing of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 这两场胜利对于所谓的共和党建制派来说都是决定性的。

sentences.en: And quickly touted signs that even in the reddest of districts, voters won't necessarily go with the most right-wing candidates.
sentences.zh: 这也迅速释放出一个信号：即使在最红的选区，选民也不一定会选择最右翼的候选人。

sentences.en: But of course, Donald Trump didn't endorse neither of those races.
sentences.zh: 但当然，唐纳德·特朗普并没有为这两场竞选背书。

sentences.en: And in all 33 races that he did, the Texas Republicans he backed won or are on track to do so.
sentences.zh: 而在他支持的所有33场竞选中，那些德克萨斯州的共和党人都赢了，或者正朝着胜利迈进。

sentences.en: There were also some signs that it can be perilous to cross Trump.
sentences.zh: 也有一些迹象表明，与特朗普作对可能是危险的。

sentences.en: Take Van Taylor.
sentences.zh: 看看Van Taylor。

sentences.en: He's a two-term incumbent congressman from up in Dallas who, just like Dan Crenshaw,
sentences.zh: 他是来自达拉斯的两届现任国会议员，就像Dan Crenshaw一样，

sentences.en: had his formerly competitive seat completely transformed into a Republican stronghold through redistricting.
sentences.zh: 他原本竞争激烈的选区通过选区重划，完全变成了共和党的铁票仓。

sentences.en: His opponents this year in the primary pounded him for voting to confirm the 2020 election results and for voting to create the January 6th commission.
sentences.zh: 他今年的初选对手猛烈抨击他投票确认2020年大选结果，并投票支持成立1月6日调查委员会。

sentences.en: Van Taylor was forced into a runoff, which is a rare outcome for an incumbent.
sentences.zh: Van Taylor被迫进入决选，这对现任议员来说是罕见的结果。

sentences.en: In the days since, a personal scandal forced him to withdraw from the race.
sentences.zh: 此后的几天里，一场个人丑闻迫使他退出了竞选。

sentences.en: Now, the seat's going to go to the other leading candidate, a Republican who centered his campaign on election fraud and attacking Van Taylor for the votes he took.
sentences.zh: 现在，这个席位将归属于另一位领先的候选人，一位将竞选核心放在选举舞弊以及攻击Van Taylor投票记录上的共和党人。

sentences.en: I spoke with Crenshaw's team yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我昨天和Crenshaw的团队谈过。

sentences.en: They told me they're hoping the results out of Texas will help, quote, shut up the congressman's critics.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们希望德克萨斯州的结果能有助于“让这位议员的批评者闭嘴”。

sentences.en: At the same time, right-wing political operatives in the area have told me they're already working to find someone who can put up a meaningful fight against Crenshaw in 2024.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当地的右翼政治操盘手告诉我，他们已经在寻找能在2024年对Crenshaw发起有力挑战的人选。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Thursday, Russian forces laid siege to urban areas across southern Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 周四，俄罗斯军队对乌克兰南部的城市地区进行了围攻，

sentences.en: striking apartment buildings, pharmacies, and a hospital as they continued to target civilian populations.
sentences.zh: 在持续针对平民人口的同时，袭击了公寓楼、药店和一家医院。

sentences.en: In the day's most alarming development, Russian forces shelled a nuclear power complex in the city of Zafirija, triggering a dangerous fire at the plan.
sentences.zh: 在当天最令人震惊的进展中，俄军炮击了扎波罗热市的一座核电站，引发了工厂内的一场危险火灾。

sentences.en: But Russian troops made little progress in overtaking the capital of Kyiv, where a miles-long convoy of soldiers and equipment remained stalled about 18 miles outside the city.
sentences.zh: 但俄军在攻占首都基辅方面进展甚微，一支长达数英里的士兵和装备车队仍停滞在离城市约18英里外的地方。

sentences.en: In televised remarks, Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected claims that his military was faring poorly in Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 在电视讲话中，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京否认了有关其军队在乌克兰表现不佳的说法，

sentences.en: saying that the war was proceeding, quote, strictly according to schedule.
sentences.zh: 称战争正在“严格按照计划”进行。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Diana Wynn和Rachel Quester制作。

sentences.zh: 由Lisa Tobin编辑，包含Dan Powell和Marion Lozano的原创音乐，并由Chris Wood进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的Jim Brunberg和Ben Lansford创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.zh: 我是Michael Bobarro。

sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正准备迎接节假日的客人。

sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会睡到不省人事。

sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？
